scope: Every case63..129, all original occurrences and full recipe snapshots, manually authored case assessments; exact owner baseline bytes inspected when present.

cases.assessment: JCM1023 and363 specify 8% w/v sodium carbonate stock, added as 2.5 mL. Frozen 2.5 G_PER_L is a volume-to-mass transcription inconsistency. The concentration-qualified stock is not CHEBI29377 sodium carbonate or an unspecified sodium carbonate solution.

TOGO API M2277 names CoCI2.6H2O in Solution2 (SL12), but separately labels the component Cobalt dichloride hexahydrate, 190 mg. This supports correcting capital I to lower-case l in CoCl2·6H2O, corroborated by CHEBI53503; the literal invalid formula is not a chemical synonym.

DSMZ1738/1739/1741 and MediaDive solutions5819/5825 specify La(NO3)3·6H2O; Sigma331937 independently gives CAS10277-43-7. The existing UNMAPPED0423 record is the same MediaDive1586 source identity with lost parentheses, not a new anhydrous lanthanum nitrate owner.

The frozen NBRC1126-derived label says KAl(SO4)2·2H2O; the original NBRC1126 ingredient table specifies KAl(SO4)2·12H2O, 0.018 g. Correct the occurrence to potassium aluminium sulfate dodecahydrate; the erroneous dihydrate literal must not resolve globally to CHEBI86465.

The AIK token uses capital I in place of aluminium Al. DSMZ141/141c/282/718 specify AlK(SO4)2·12H2O directly; DSMZ935b references medium141 mineral solution. TOGO API fields identify aluminium potassium sulfate dodecahydrate. Hydration stays twelve, and the invalid element token is not a resolving chemical synonym.

JCM386/714 add commercial Middlebrook OADC enrichment separately from basal medium; it is the oleic-acid/albumin/dextrose/catalase supplement class. Existing OADC_Enrichment is a preparation owner, but its Difco synonym and absent formulation cannot prove BD-BBL exact product interchangeability.

Paraamino specifies the amino group para to the benzoic-acid carboxyl group, matching CHEBI30753 4-aminobenzoic acid. Both TOGO3160/3161 frozen vitamin contexts preserve this unqualified acid; no salt, stock or other isomer qualifier is present.

The frozen label explicitly denotes 0.2% w/v ferrous sulfate heptahydrate stock. Current DSMZ503 instead describes 0.1% ferrous sulfate stock, a source-version/concentration discrepancy. Neither liquid stock is identical to a pure heptahydrate ingredient.

NBRC223 explicitly supplies Fe2(SO4)3·(NH4)2SO4·24H2O. Reducing the entire double formula by two gives NH4Fe(SO4)2·12H2O. Sigma F3629 confirms ferric ammonium sulfate dodecahydrate/CAS7783-83-7. NLM MeSH M0141705 specifically denotes ammonium ferric sulfate dodecahydrate, distinct from descriptor C049467 and its anhydrous preferred concept. Select the exact M concept. TOGO M1451 incorrectly labels the raw ferric formula iron(II), which must not override source/supplier stoichiometry.

NBRC1025 explicitly repeats Fe2(SO4)3·6H2O. It is ferric sulfate with six waters per diiron-trisulfate formula unit, distinct from ferrous sulfate and variable-hydrate iron(III) sulfate. The source gives no catalogue/CAS identifying the fixed hydrate.

NBRC109 YPAD specifies adenine sulfate, 40 mg; the second TOGO2239 occurrence also lacks a catalogue or hydration qualifier. SigmaA2545 establishes adenine hemisulfate as a commercial candidate, but a name-only sulfate entry does not establish its hydrate state or supplier formulation. Free adenine is not this salt.

The frozen26 occurrences restore MediaDB C00002 as generic ATP/CHEBI15422. However, the original Merlen1999 Table1, personally inspected as a rendered PDF, specifies ATP (Na2),0.36 micromolar in CDM/LP (CultureMech:007240); the frozen0.00036mM is the same quantity but has lost the disodium supplied form. KEGG C00002 and CHEBI15422 describe the generic ATP molecule and cannot erase that counterion. The remaining25 Zahorchak-derived occurrences correspond to the original paper, whose seven primary scanned pages953-959 were retrieved and visually inspected after an initial PDF-path failure. The article names ATP but does not establish the ordinary supplied ATP counterion or product; its separately described radiolabeled ATP reagent does not establish the unlabeled reagent salt. The earlier global neutral-ATP new-owner proposal is withdrawn and archived; this aggregate must be split or retain a supplied-form hold.

JCM1146/1147/1176/1415 explicitly use 50% v/v methanol stocks, with differing addition volumes; JCM1173 is currently unavailable. Percent by volume is part of the stock identity, not a purity synonym of methanol.

TOGO API M2262 independently carries malformed component_name Cd(NO3).4H2O but separately labels GMO002395 Cadmium nitrate tetrahydrate. The named material supports correcting the source formula to Cd(NO3)2·4H2O; the literal missing-nitrate string is not valid exact identity.

UTEX modified P-IV/DAS context identifies Sigma H7154. The manufacturer explicitly identifies HEEDTA/HEDTA free acid, CAS150-39-0, C10H18N2O7. NLM MeSH M0085998 specifically denotes N-(hydroxyethyl)ethylenediaminetriacetic acid. Use that exact free-acid concept, not umbrella C026060 whose separate narrower concepts represent sodium/calcium/potassium salts and metal chelates. No salt labels are imported as synonyms; this is neither EDTA nor trisodium HEDTA.

DSMZ732/732a solution B and MediaDive1488/1497 explicitly enumerate (NH4)2CO3 as a weighed constituent. CHEBI229630 describes diammonium carbonate. Balanced parentheses recover the exact ammonium carbonate formula behind existing NH42CO3; the component remains separate from its stock solution.

The original ATCC recipe says Se-Salt (Na selenite), 0.5 g. Sodium selenite is a plausible disodium selenite parent, but the recipe does not identify supplied hydration or a catalogue. The candidate owner CHEBI48843 is explicitly disodium selenite and cannot establish the omitted supplied form by itself.

NBRC213 adds 2.5 mL of FeSO4 (0.02 M) to a buffer. The label denotes a molar stock without specifying which crystalline hydrate prepared it; exact identity with ferrous sulfate heptahydrate would invent material provenance.

The MediaDive P4 occurrence is a nested ingredient of an AgNO3 stock, not the stock node itself. Its frozen composition is 1 g/L, equivalent to the source 1 mg/mL stock strength. The formula AgNO3 agrees with CHEBI32130 silver(1+) nitrate, CAS7761-88-8. Propose the solute owner only; this does not approve an inferred final-medium dose.

FeSO4(NH4)2SO4.6H2O has one Fe, two ammonium ions, two sulfate ions and six waters, exactly ferrous ammonium sulfate hexahydrate CHEBI76181. TOGO2560 context names this weighed compound; grouping order does not change the salt.

JCM987 explicitly adds 50 mL of 10% MgSO4·7H2O preparation. The percentage-qualified liquid is a stock prepared from heptahydrate, not a synonym of crystalline magnesium sulfate heptahydrate. The printed percent basis is not further invented.

PIPES (Sigma) supplies a manufacturer but no catalogue. The original JCM997 endpoint currently returns no recipe. CHEBI39033 is a PIPES umbrella term and has salt children; the existing owner also carries free-acid chemistry. An unspecified vendor name cannot independently choose free acid versus a PIPES salt.

Both NBRC830 and831 explicitly print (NH4)2SO4·7H2O, so the unusual heptahydrate string is not merely a downstream transcription error. Neither source supplies material characterization or a catalogue. Silently deleting waters would collapse a claimed supplied form.

TOGO API M2231 explicitly gives MgSO4·7H2O (6 g/L) as a 5 mL addition. The frozen 5 G_PER_L field is therefore a source-unit transcription error, while 6 g/L is the stock strength. The heptahydrate solute remains distinct from the measured stock solution.

Fe(SO4)·7H2O contains a redundant sulfate parenthesis and exactly matches iron(II) sulfate heptahydrate CHEBI75836. TOGO3155 frozen notes aggregate two additions; chemical aliasing does not approve the merged 0.05+0.8 g quantities or preparation stages.
JCM363 explicitly lists 0.1% w/v resazurin-Na, 1 mL. This is a sodium-salt stock at a defined mass/volume strength, not free-acid resazurin CHEBI8806. Both salt and stock qualifiers are meaningful.

(NH4)2SO4FeSO4 ×6H2O is the additive formula of the same ferrous ammonium sulfate hexahydrate as CHEBI76181. TOGO3118 separately names the iron and nickel double salts, preventing cross-metal conflation.
DSMZ29/40 use 2 N sulfuric acid as a prepared acid reagent in pH adjustment. Normality qualifies the stock and depends on an equivalent basis; the liquid is not pure H2SO4.

Original DSMZ1250 lists Ca(NO3)2·4H2O whereas the frozen TOGO2531 label says five waters. The primary recipe supports a source-bound correction to calcium nitrate tetrahydrate. It does not make a five-water formula an exact synonym of the tetrahydrate.

TOGO API M412 explicitly defines Sol.3 as NaHCO3 2 g with 40 mL water and a 5% annotation, and adds 40 mL to main solution. JCM414 instructs adding filter-sterilized 5% bicarbonate solution after combining the separately autoclaved fractions. The local reference is therefore resolved to the bicarbonate stock in this recipe; it is not a global chemical name.

JCM1023 prints 0.1% w/v resazurin-Na; frozen resazurin--Na adds a typographic hyphen. The source correction stays within the sodium-salt stock, preserving 0.1% w/v and its dose; it cannot be imported as a free-acid resazurin synonym.

JCM673 explicitly specifies Fe2(SO4)3·xH2O. Variable x and n both leave water stoichiometry unspecified and match the existing local variable-ferric-sulfate-hydrate identity. The broad CHEBI53438 parent remains asymmetric and does not identify a fixed hydrate.

TOGO1217 freezes calcium nitrate with six waters. JCM1137 currently has no retrievable recipe; a related MediaDive5240 also repeats six waters, which corroborates the string but does not establish a characterized supplied form. Tetrahydrate must not be substituted from prevalence.

(NH4)2Fe(SO4)2·6H2O directly specifies Mohr salt, CHEBI76181. Original JCM950/966 both list 2.0 mg of this salt, corroborated by TOGO M997/M1016. The frozen G_PER_L unit must not be inherited as if the original 2 mg addition were grams. Identity aliasing preserves six waters and does not approve recipe unit flattening.

Four MediaDB yeast contexts specify BDH silicone antifoam. Verduyn1992-derived records dose 0.025 mL/L, while Flikweert1996-derived records use 0.05 mL/L in the demineralized-water input. Manufacturer/formulation and preparation stage matter; a proprietary silicone emulsion is not a single siloxane compound. Primary Delft full-text retrieval attempts failed.

The original NIES SOT recipe footnote explicitly replaces 250 mg MnSO4·7H2O by 217 mg MnSO4·5H2O. The frozen trailing 1 ) is the footnote marker, not a molecular constituent. The pentahydrate identity is supported, but the decorated raw token should be corrected at the occurrence rather than globally exported.

JCM1182 explicitly names Cr2(SO4)3·xH2O in its trace solution. Chromium(III) sulfate is the salt skeleton, but x is unspecified; neither an anhydrous exact mapping nor an invented fixed water count is justified.

DSMZ280 supplies trimethylamine-HCl; CHEBI64700 is equimolar trimethylamine hydrochloride. The multiplication separator in Trimethylamine x HCl denotes the same salt. Existing Methylamine-HCl EXACT_SYNONYM is a different one-carbon amine salt (CHEBI59337/CAS593-51-1), not three-carbon trimethylamine hydrochloride (CAS593-81-7); preserve but reject the wrong alias.

TOGO API M2790 M9 context explicitly supplies 1 M MgSO4 as 200 microlitres. This contradicts the frozen 200 G_PER_L transcription and establishes a stock addition, not a crystalline supplied form. Neither magnesium sulfate nor its heptahydrate can own the complete stock name exactly.

TOGO2313 specifies larch-derived arabinogalactan as an alternative carbon material at 0.2%, with percentage basis unspecified for this addition. CHEBI27569 is generic arabinogalactan; the existing (+)-arabinogalactan owner lacks botanical provenance and composition establishing exact larch material equivalence.

The original ATCC source defines selenite-tungstate solution with NaOH0.5 g, Na2SeO3·5H2O3 mg, Na2WO4·2H2O4 mg in water1 L. This is a specific alkaline trace mixture; other named selenite-tungstate recipes differ and cannot be merged solely by the compound pair.

The original ATCC medium adds 0.4 mL of 0.2% FeSO4·7H2O stock. Percentage is part of the preparation; the printed source does not explicitly give w/v, so that basis is not supplied from another recipe.

UTEX Minor Nutrients prints NiSO4(NH4)SO4 x6H2O but names Sigma574988. That manufacturer catalogue explicitly specifies (NH4)2Ni(SO4)2·6H2O, CAS7785-20-8/CHEBI86149. The missing ammonium subscript is thus source-correctable; the incorrect literal must not become an exact synonym.

DSMZ897 uses 2 N sulfuric acid for pH adjustment and DSMZ206 uses it in sulfide preparation. Both designate acid stocks; different process uses do not convert their source labels into pure sulfuric-acid aliases.

MediaDive solution5240 explicitly repeats Ca(NO3)2 x6H2O with compound2013, while JCM1137 is currently unavailable. A repeated database string is not independent proof of a stable hexahydrate; the exact supplied form remains unverified.

JCM355/1201/1330 all define the below-referenced rumen preparation by heat treatment followed by centrifugation, and explicitly call the resulting material clarified rumen fluid. The see below text is a procedural pointer; source-proven clarification matches the existing biological preparation owner without asserting a fixed molecular composition.

NBRC869 prints Dithionite (ca.) as approximately20 mg and discusses a dithionite solution. The parenthetical ca. is consistent with circa, not a formula for calcium. The source never specifies a sodium/calcium counterion, so neither salt can be selected exactly.
NBRC1379 solutionII dissolves FeSO4·7H2O400 g in 1 L of 0.25 N H2SO4. The named sulfuric acid is the stock solvent, not pure acid and not the resulting iron solution.

TOGO2241 explicitly qualifies H2SO4 as concd. This denotes a concentrated commercial acid reagent with no stated assay. The missing concentration is substantive and cannot be removed by matching the H2SO4 substring.

NBRC1004/1390 both specify desiccated ox bile, an animal-derived dry preparation. Existing UNMAPPED0374 Desicatted Ox-bile describes the same material class with a spelling error; generic bile acids or liquid bile would lose the supplied preparation.

ATCC920 uses concentrated sulfuric acid in a micronutrient preparation; JCM970 is currently unavailable and TOGO3140 supplies no additional assay. All occurrences retain the concentrated liquid qualifier. A pure sulfuric-acid parent does not capture its supplied strength.

DSMZ991/1005 and ATCC use 10 N H2SO4 as a pH titrant; JCM92 explicitly lists 1 mL, while JCM382 is unavailable. The normality-qualified reagent is a stock across all frozen occurrences, not an exact pure-acid alias.

DSMZ996 itself prints Ni2SO4x6H2O, so the extra nickel coefficient is not solely a downstream error. CHEBI53437 nickel(II) sulfate hexahydrate is plausible, but the literal formula does not balance the usual Ni2+/SO4 ratio. Source repetition alone cannot validate the repair.
The original ATCC formulation uses H2SO4 (conc.) as 0.05 mL in a 100 mL iron stock. This is concentrated acid reagent, not the finished iron stock and not assay-free pure H2SO4.

DSMZ1113 separately adds 100 mL Leptospira Enrichment EMJH and 2.3 g Leptospira Medium Base EMJH. This directly contradicts mapping the enrichment to the existing basal-medium owner. The commercial supplement is a mixture with its own product identity.

TOGO3239 Kim medium specifies 10N H2SO4. Missing whitespace changes no normality qualifier; the intended item remains a prepared acid reagent. No original source assay/preparation is available to claim more.

JCM764 explicitly lists 0.2% Fe(NH4)2(SO4)2·6H2O in 0.037% HCl, 1 mL. This is an acidified Mohr-salt stock with two specified solutes; the entire preparation is not equivalent to crystalline CHEBI76181.

NBRC840 itself prints Fe(NH4)2SO4·6H2O with only one sulfate; it does not match charge-balanced Mohr salt. A missing sulfate subscript is plausible but remains a source error hypothesis without supplier or independent formula evidence.

TOGO API M2196 itself repeats Mg2SO4.7H2O while labeling the row Magnesium sulfate heptahydrate, 0.1 g. The extra Mg makes the formula charge-inconsistent and contradicts the source semantic label. The legacy MediaIngredientMech identifier in the frozen context is not independent source proof.

TOGO API M2405 BSM9:1 LB prints (NH4)SO4 and separately labels the 2.38 g row Ammonium sulfate. The missing ammonium multiplier is not charge-balanced conventional ammonium sulfate. A general LB preparation page cannot resolve the contradictory formula or supplied form.

(NH4)2SO4NiSO4 ×6H2O has two ammonium ions, one nickel, two sulfate ions and six waters, matching CHEBI86149. TOGO3118 names a nickel double salt separately from the ferrous analogue. Use the explicit hexahydrate owner; a second file sharing the ID has an unhydrated label and does not establish interchangeability.

The available JCM324/368/369/417/419/478/508/523/524/592 recipes explicitly specify Fe2(SO4)3·xH2O; JCM413/603 are currently unavailable. This matches the local variable-ferric-sulfate-hydrate identity, not a fixed hydrate or anhydrous CHEBI53438. JCM369 acidified-stock instructions do not erase solute-versus-stock grouping.

Fe(III)NH4-EDTA explicitly includes ammonium, distinct from ferric EDTA anion and sodium ferric EDTA. DSMZ632/1181 list weighed material, while DSMZ1132/MediaDive2271 dose 1 mL, so the same label spans compound and liquid-stock occurrences. One global exact identity would conceal this stage/form distinction.

The ATCC chopped-meat carbohydrate formulation adds 4 mL Resazurin Soln (0.025%). The source does not identify free acid versus sodium salt or the percent basis. Stock concentration is explicit and cannot be stripped during chemical matching.

UTEX BBM Bold trace stock uses concentrated sulfuric acid, 10 mL per litre of trace preparation. The frozen CHEBI26836 annotation identifies the solute only and cannot establish concentration-qualified stock identity or a molarity inferred from density.

DSMZ996 explicitly lists H2SeO3 (selenous acid), 10 mg, and CHEBI26642 independently identifies selenous acid. The parenthetical name spells out the same H2SeO3 compound; it does not add a salt, hydration or stock qualifier.

The frozen JCM448-derived Mg(NO3)·6H2O lacks the second nitrate. Original JCM448 explicitly lists Mg(NO3)2·6H2O, 2.54 g, supporting correction to magnesium nitrate hexahydrate. The malformed formula must not become a globally resolving exact synonym.
